thread:
jules: Quick q — thinking about adding a new manifest field 'compat_level' + an 'abi_tag' to short-circuit heavy benchmarking at intake. Idea: run fast structural checks (shapes/dtypes/kv layout) before full bench. Thoughts?

ashwin: 👍 in principle. How would levels look? auto-infer from artifacts or user-specified in manifest?

jules: Proposal: compat_level = one of [strict, compat, skip]. strict = full bench+eval, compat = ABI/shape checks + microbench, skip = only smoke. Default to compat for internal builds. Fail fast on ABI mismatch.

maria: Concern: users might set skip and bypass safety. Need policy: external/public ingest should not be allowed skip. Also we need audit log that records who set level.

ben: Agreed. Implementation note: intake can enforce policy per org. Also we should keep a lightweight microbench that verifies p50/p95 and basic token throughput against a golden baseline.

carmen: Microbench-sled idea: run 3 short sequences per variant, 3 seeds each, compare p50/p95 and token/sec with thresholds. Save the exact input seeds and random state in the manifest for reproducibility.

ci-bot: [deploy] microbench-sled service rolled to staging — default timeout 5m, concurrency 4 (reacts :rocket:).

ashwin: For ABI checks we don't need to instantiate full model weights. We can parse meta tensors and verify shapes/order/contiguity: num_heads * head_dim, ln param shapes, kv cache expected dims. Small validator binary should do.

jules: Exactly. Example manifest snippet I'm thinking: 
```yaml
compat_level: compat
abi_tag: "kv-v1|ln-v2"
microbench:
  inputs: ["golden_short.jsonl"]
  sequences: [16, 64, 128]
```

maria: We also need surface in Console: which check failed, human-readable hints (e.g., "expected kv dim 64 but found 32"), links to remediation docs. No one likes opaque failures.

ben: And an automatic remediation flow: if ABI fails, create internal ticket to runtime-abi-team with model fingerprint + failing tensors. That will speed triage.

carmen: Edge case: quantized artifacts. Dtype may match but kernel codepaths differ and perf/regressions happen. Add a dequant smoke: run small int8 decode & compare logits/tokens with tolerant thresholds.

jules: Also add 'bench_intents' in manifest (chat|completion|embed) so microbench picks representative inputs. Saves us from generic sequences that don't match workload.

ashwin: Rollout plan suggestion: 1) land manifest schema + validator as opt-in, 2) require compat_level for external/public intakes, 3) after one-week opt-in telemetry, flip default to stricter.

maria: Local DX: provide a CLI lint: `rictl model lint .` that runs same validators locally and prints actionable hints. Helps speed up iteration.

jules: +1. Also on Console show model badge: green/amber/red with timestamped check artifacts and ability to re-run checks on demand.

ben: Concern: onboarding latency/cost. If microbench-sled runs up to 5m per variant, cost scales. Mitigation: parallelize, cap concurrency per-account, and sample variants (fp32 + one quant) first.

carmen: Alternate: mark model provisional after fast checks and schedule full bench asynchronously. If a full bench fails, rollback rollout and notify.

ashwin: Good compromise. Action items: jules -> open manifest schema PR + example, ashwin -> validator lib skeleton, maria -> console UI spec, ben -> infra cost estimate + concurrency plan, carmen -> microbench input set + seeds. Aim for POC next Wed?

jules: I'll open the PR today and ping owners. TY all.
